To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
combined immunotherapy with L. monocytogenes-based prostate cancer vaccine and radiation therapy causes a significant regression of established prostate cancer in mice.
combined immunotherapy with ADXS31-42 and radiation therapy (RT) leads to a significant therapeutic response in a mouse model for prostate cancer.
the combined immunotherapy with RT using Listeria PSA vaccines and radiation therapy leads significantly to a therapeutic response of PSA-specific T cells in a murine tumor model of prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new treatment strategy for prostate cancer using a combination of immunotherapy and RT.
the development of new therapeutic approaches to prostate cancer.
a combination therapy using a Listeria vaccine with RT to treat prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
combined immunotherapy with ADXS31-42 and radiation therapy leads in a murine prostate cancer model to a therapeutic response.
combined treatment with RT and Lm-based immunotherapy leads to a significant increase in PSA-specific immune response that results in a complete regression of the established tumors.

combination immunotherapy with L. monocytogenes vaccine (ADXS-31-142) and RT causes complete regression of established prostate cancer and this effect is mediated by the augmentation of the PSA-specific CTL responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
combination of radiation and immunotherapy with a Listeria vaccine is a novel approach to prostate cancer therapy that warrants further investigation.
the combination of RT with Listeria vaccine is an effective treatment for prostate cancer.
combination therapy with RT and immunotherapy with a Listeria PSA-based vaccine can cause tumor regression by augmentation of PSA-specific CTLs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of immunotherapy with L. monocytogenes vaccine and radiation therapy is an efficient therapeutic regimen for prostate cancer and this combination therapy could be a potential approach in prostate cancer treatment.
combination therapy with RT and ADXS31- 142 vaccine leads to a significant tumor growth inhibition and complete regression of established prostate cancer.
combining immunotherapy with radiation therapy can have significant therapeutic effects in prostate cancer.
